episodes.213156: The season's first rendition of the North American Monsoon high developed over south-central and southwestern NM with increased low-level moisture intruding beneath it. Faster westerly flow along the northern periphery of the high allowed for some convective organization and stronger afternoon thunderstorms. Relatively warm conditions and low humidity also allowed for strong downdrafts to occur yielding severe wind gusts from decaying thunderstorms mainly over western and central NM each day. Several of these dry downbursts produced blowing dust with one particular event resulting in zero visibility in Rio Rancho on the 25th. Storms through central and eastern NM were wetter in nature threatening locally heavy rainfall and flash flooding. Flash flooding was reported in Raton on the 24th, with another report of heavy rains producing a landslide from steep terrain near Jemez Springs along NM Highway 4 on the 26th. Other storms produced various severe wind gusts and hail across portions of northern and central NM each day.
episodes.213173: A strong upper trough moved east toward the area that helped to produce severe thundertorms over a good portion of the CWA. Flooding also occurred in parts of the area.
episodes.213187: Several rounds of thunderstorms occurred during the period of June 25th and June 27th as a frontal boundary remained near the area. Some areas received 3-6 inches of rainfall over a short period of time. Thunderstorms produced a few tornadoes on the evening of June 26th.
episodes.213188: Several rounds of thunderstorms occurred during the period of June 25th and June 27th as a frontal boundary remained near the area. Some areas received 3-6 inches of rainfall over a short period of time.
episodes.213388: On the 27th afternoon to early evening, a stationary west-east frontal boundary combined with a very moist column and forcing from a short wave trough over the Middle Mississippi Valley, to produce heavy to extreme rainfall rates over Sullivan and Greene Counties, and later Martin County.  Resultant flash flooding was considerable during the afternoon east of Sullivan through the Linton area.  Less impactful early evening flash flooding occurred in Martin County.
episodes.213390: A weak upper shortwave moved through the area during the afternoon of 6/27. With a moderate to strong destabilization with MLCAPE approaching 2000 J/kg, scattered thunderstorms developed across the area. A favorable downburst environment was in place with strong low level lapse rates and DCAPE between 700-800 J/kg. While most downbursts were sub-severe, one storm reached severe limits.
episodes.213694: A weak thunderstorm produced severe wind gusts along Interstate 80 during the evening hours of June 26th.
episodes.213695: Severe thunderstorms produced isolated and brief strong wind gusts during the late afternoon and evening hours of June 26th in western Nebraska. Flash flooding was also reported near Scottsbluff and Bridgeport Nebraska.
episodes.213839: A cold front pulled moist air into the region during the early portions of June 26th.  Morning clouds gave way during the afternoon, which allowed for the atmosphere to become more unstable. Thunderstorms initially developed in northeastern New Mexico and moved into the Panhandles during the evening and overnight of June 26th. As they encountered the moist, unstable air, they strengthened and organized into a fast-moving squall line. Damaging straight line winds were the main threat with these storms. A few storms ahead of the squall line were able to produce large hail but overall the atmosphere was not as conducive for large hail given the potential for melting to occur.
episodes.213840: A cold front pulled moist air into the region during the early portions of June 26th.  Morning clouds gave way during the afternoon, which allowed for the atmosphere to become more unstable. Thunderstorms initially developed in northeastern New Mexico and moved into the Panhandles during the evening and overnight of June 26th. As they encountered the moist, unstable air, they strengthened and organized into a fast-moving squall line. Damaging straight line winds were the main threat with these storms. A few storms ahead of the squall line were able to produce large hail but overall the atmosphere was not as conducive for large hail given the potential for melting to occur.
episodes.213991: Thunderstorms developed across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 26th, along and south of a stationary front that stretched across southern Kansas and northern Oklahoma. Locally heavy rainfall from this activity resulted in isolated flash flooding.
episodes.213992: Thunderstorms developed across northeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 26th, along and south of a stationary front that stretched across southern Kansas and northern Oklahoma. Some of these thunderstorms developed east and southeast into northwestern Arkansas during the early morning hours of the 27th, the strongest of which produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.214108: A weak short wave trough tracked across the higher terrain along the New Mexico/Colorado border during the evening of the 26th. Large scale ascent from this short wave along with low level convergence in a surface pressure trough in eastern New Mexico initiated thunderstorms during the evening hours across eastern New Mexico. This initial thunderstorm activity generated a strong outflow boundary which then moved into the South Plains of West Texas. A very dry lower atmosphere allowed these storms to produce widespread severe wind gusts as they tracked eastward across the South Plains and extreme southern Texas Panhandle through the early morning hours of the 27th.
episodes.214182: A coastal trough combined with the daily seabreeze and a second inland trough to produce multiple rounds of shower and thunderstorm activity through the day and into the evening hours on June twenty-seventh. With ample instability and deep layer shear in place some of these thunderstorms became strong to severe in nature bringing a strong and damaging wind threat to the waters mainly north of the Crystal Coast.
episodes.214241: Multiple mesoscale convective vortices triggered a line of storms that brought damaging wind gusts the New River Valley and the Piedmont. Mesoscale conditions were not the most ideal for severe weather development. Bulk shear struggled to get above 20 knots, mid-level lapse rates were about 5.5 C/km, and DAPE only up went up 500 J/kg. However, sufficient surface heating and moisture resulted in CAPE of at least 1000 J/kg which allowed for some decent thunderstorm development after the MCV trigger. There was one notable storm that brought down a swath of trees in Roanoke County and went straight eastward and brought more trees down in Charlotte County. Broad rotation was noted in the SRV data by the time it reached Charlotte County with a 59.3 mph velocity gate recorded at around 7250 feet.
episodes.214357: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a weak surface front/pressure trough across northern Oklahoma on the evening of the 26th. This activity produced damaging winds, hail and flooding as it progressed south/southeastward into the early morning of the 27th. Significant damaging winds and hail were noted with a trio of more organized thunderstorms (supercells) during this time impacting areas around Enid, Stillwater, Oklahoma City and Chandler, OK.
episodes.214491: Isolated thunderstorms tracked across north central and northeast Colorado with wind gusts up to 68 mph and hail up to one inch in diameter.
episodes.214611: The area was beneath a deep area of high pressure resulting in light wind fields.  A lake breeze boundary developed due to differential heating between the lake and nearby land and convection initiated along this boundary.  One of the storms produced a strong marine thunderstorm winds in Lake Pontchartrain.
episodes.214701: An upper level low over the PAC northwest and along British Columbia coastline, pushed southward into Nevada. This system brought isolated to scattered  thunderstorms across northern Nevada with strong winds across central Nevada. Temperatures dropped to near freezing over the weekend.
episodes.214820: Weak surface high pressure ridging was centered just to the south of the JAX CWA on both the 26th and 27th, resulting in a west to southwest flow across the region. Sufficient moisture and summertime instability resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms, with some strong to severe storms causing isolated reports of damage across the area.
episodes.214972: A warm front lifted across North Dakota while strong southerly surface flow increased temperatures and dew points over the region. As a surface trough tracked to the east, storms developed in eastern Montana and moved into western North Dakota during the evening. Storms quickly formed a line as they continued moving east-northeast, with powerful wind gusts the primary hazard across western and portions of central North Dakota. A tornado occurred approximately 7 miles north-northeast of Belfield in Billings County. The track was less than one mile long and wind speeds were estimated up to 90 mph, leading to an EF-1 rating. Damaging wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph were common across the area as storms moved through. The most significant damage occurred in a neighborhood west of Williston. The Emergency Manager reported debris in a southwest to northeast orientation, consistent with straight line winds. Notable damage includes two homes with roofs uplifted and partially blown off. Other damage includes sheds, enclosed trailers, and campers damaged or destroyed. Some tree damage was also noted. Damage is consistent with wind speeds around 95 mph.
episodes.215019: Severe thunderstorms impacted portions of western SD with large hail, damaging wind gusts and reports of minor damage.
episodes.215026: Multiple rounds of severe weather impacted much of western SD and the eastern Plains. Biggest threat was large hail which was confirmed by numerous chaser reports. Damaging wind gusts were also measured by SD mesonet stations and personal weather stations across the area.
episodes.215145: A stationary front was draped from the Ohio Valley into the northern Mid-Atlantic region. A mid-level system tracked in from the west and led to numerous showers and storms across the Coastal Plain and Piedmont of Central North Carolina. Numerous wind damage reports were observed.
episodes.215167: Mainly zonal flow aloft with embedded low amplitude perturbations resulted in scattered thunderstorm development across southeastern Virginia. Isolated severe storms occurred.
episodes.215168: Mainly zonal flow aloft with embedded low amplitude perturbations resulted in scattered thunderstorm development across North Carolina. These storms produced gusty winds as they moved over the North Carolina coastal waters.
episodes.215313: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed across western North Carolina throughout the afternoon. Several of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215315: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over upstate South Carolina throughout the afternoon. A few of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215325: Scattered thunderstorms developed along an outflow boundary and north of a warm front during the afternoon of June 27th.  Storms were most numerous south of I-70.  One brief tornado touched down in Crawford County while several funnel clouds occurred further north along the outflow boundary.  Pockets of heavy rain led to a few flash flood reports, with the most significant in Charleston in Coles County.
episodes.215335: Persistent thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall caused flash flooding in Marion County in the early afternoon.
episodes.215380: The combination of a passing shortwave and a strong jet moving over western and central Wyoming brought numerous severe thunderstorms, with strong wind the main hazard from the storms. Some wind gusts reached hurricane force, with the strongest gust of 89 mph along Interstate 90 to the east of Buffalo in Johnson County. A 77 mph wind gust was reported in western Sublette County. Wind gusts over 58 mph also occurred in Fremont, Lincoln, Washakie, Park and Hot Springs Counties.
episodes.215503: A strong thunderstorm generated a brief funnel cloud on June 26. It was reported by public with no damage.
episodes.215625: A cluster of thunderstorms moved east to southeast across Yuma and Kit Carson Counties during the evening hours on the 26th. Ping-pong ball size hail and a 68 mph measured wind gust were both reported in Cheyenne County.
episodes.215631: During the late evening hours on the 26th, eastward-moving decaying showers and thunderstorms south of Logan County produced a measured 69 mph wind gust over far southwest portions of Logan County.
episodes.215662: Thunderstorms developed across southeast Kansas and adjacent areas of northern Oklahoma. These thunderstorms were nearly stationary, especially across portions of Montgomery County. This produced tremendous rainfall and a few reports of flash-flooding.
episodes.215756: Persistent enhanced westerly flow with multiple embedded shortwave troughs brought multiple instances of severe wind gusts and hail to northern Utah as well as flash flooding to Sevier county.
episodes.215792: A few pop up thunderstorms developed in the afternoon over Delaware, producing damaging wind gusts and frequent lightning.
episodes.215883: Hot and humid conditions under high pressure led to a typical summertime environment capable of supporting strong pulse-type thunderstorms across Southeast South Carolina.
episodes.215961: One inch hail fell in Clifton.
episodes.215973: Multiple rounds of storms occurred June 26-28th, 2026 resulting in significant flash flooding over southern Indiana and central Kentucky as well as an EF-0 tornado.  Several flash flood warnings were issued over the 2 day period with Considerable Flash Flooding in multiple locations and even Flash Flood Emergencies in some areas. Rainfall totals for the weekend ended up in an area wide 2-4 inches with swaths of 6-10+ inches!!  Unfortunately 3 fatalities were confirmed due to flooding in Madison County, KY, and 1 fatality indirectly related to the flooding occurred on Floyds Fork in Jefferson County, KY.
episodes.216004: Multiple rounds of storms occurred June 26-28th, 2026 resulting in significant flash flooding over southern Indiana and central Kentucky as well as an EF-0 tornado.  Several flash flood warnings were issued over the 2 day period with Considerable Flash Flooding in multiple locations and even Flash Flood Emergencies in some areas.  Rainfall totals for the weekend ended up in an area wide 2-4 inches with swaths of 6-10+ inches.
episodes.216036: Following a morning cold front, clearing skies allowed for weak to moderate instability (500-1000 j/kg of CAPE) to build in across SW Idaho. With an upper trough just to the west, dynamics and kinematics were favorable for thunderstorm development. The 00z sounding that afternoon revealed a precipitable water value of 0.96 inches, well above the 90th percentile value of 0.83 inches. With high moisture values, heavy rain was a threat with any storms that developed.
episodes.216101: Storms coming off the mountains of southern MT and northern WY produced hail up to 2 in diameter and gusts up to 70 mph.
episodes.216102: Storms coming off the mountains of southern MT and northern WY produced hail up to 2 in diameter and gusts up to 70 mph.
